title: Policy probe
blurb: Constructs RTCPeerConnection instances with every RTCRtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy value (omitted, disable, negotiate, require, bogus), reads getConfiguration(), probes the build's accepted enum vocabulary, and tests setConfiguration() immutability.
question: Which RTCRtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy enum values does this browser accept, what does getConfiguration() reflect by default, and does setConfiguration() reject post-construction policy changes with InvalidModificationError?
result: In Chrome 153 headless, unflagged builds omit rtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy (0/10 conformance); with --enable-blink-features=RtcRtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy, default is 'negotiate', 'require' reflects, 'bogus' and 'disable' throw TypeError (pre webrtc-extensions PR #256), and setConfiguration() does not throw InvalidModificationError (7/10 conformance). Full Chrome 160 behavior including 'disable' not yet verified.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (unflagged and --enable-blink-features=RtcRtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy); not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Chrome 153 behind RtcRtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy rejects 'disable' with TypeError because it predates webrtc-extensions PR #256
friction.repro: Run new RTCPeerConnection({ rtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy: 'disable' }) in Chrome 153 with --enable-blink-features=RtcRtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy; WebIDL enum conversion throws TypeError because only 'negotiate' and 'require' are registered.
friction.workaround: Probe each policy value inside a try/catch block rather than assuming 'disable' is accepted on every flagged Chromium build.

friction.summary: RTCPeerConnection.setConfiguration() silently accepts a changed rtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy in Chrome 153 instead of throwing InvalidModificationError
friction.repro: Create new RTCPeerConnection({ rtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy: 'require' }) with the flag on in Chrome 153 and call pc.setConfiguration({ rtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy: 'negotiate' }); it resolves without throwing InvalidModificationError.
friction.workaround: Treat rtpHeaderEncryptionPolicy as construction-only and create a new RTCPeerConnection if the security policy must change.
